features.title: Ranked @ mentions for files and threads
features.summary: One @ menu that interleaves local files and threads plus this DSH's remote threads by match quality, recency, and workspace or project; @thread: / @t: and @file: / @f: narrow results, and picks insert native reference chips.
reach: fill textbox "Describe what you want to build, / commands, @ files or sessions" "Seed a mention target"
fill textbox "Describe what you want to build, / commands, @ files or sessions" "@t:"
failureModes: A failed Host lookup drops that kind of candidate and keeps the other one.
A missing multi-host API keeps local file and thread candidates available.
A quoted path cannot keep its scope prefix through a drill, so it continues as a plain @ mention.

verification.testName: reads the long and short scope prefixes and keeps what was typed
puts an exact thread title above a fuzzy file match
interleaves files and threads of the same tier instead of listing one kind first
caps the menu and ranks 500 entries in well under a frame
offers recorded remote threads as native mentions and omits absent or blank sessions

features.title: Referenced threads open on click
features.summary: A thread chip in the composer, the thread chip in a sent message and its "Referenced session · …" line open that thread. With @dshfiles/main-tabs the thread opens per the tabs openMode setting, and Cmd/Ctrl-click always opens a new tab.
reach: fill textbox "Describe what you want to build, / commands, @ files or sessions" "@t:"
failureModes: A reference line naming a thread that is no longer listed stays inert.
Without @dshfiles/main-tabs, or with its tabs off, Cmd/Ctrl-click opens the thread like a plain click.

verification.testName: reads the session id out of a canonical mention and ignores anything else
maps labels to the sessions a thread referenced, the latest reference winning
finds the clicked label in a "Referenced session" line
opens a Mod-clicked thread in a new tab even in preview mode, and navigates to it

telemetry.reason: Client-only: Referenced threads open on click renders browser state and starts no Host work of its own.
